(i) A group-aware temporal protocol (B2) partitions the dataset into ten contiguous TimeUS blocks and evaluates over ten seeds, eliminating the inflation produced by random stratified splits that mix neighbouring samples. (ii) A three-mode feature audit (full/loose/strict) quantifies how much accuracy stems from instantaneous physical signals versus contextual proxies (cumulative energy, battery state, GPS trajectory). (iii) A hybrid XGBoost + Data Reuploading (DRU) classifier is benchmarked against five paired non-linear controls (raw, PCA, polynomial-2, random-RBF, and an untrained DRU map) under identical budgets. The standalone DRU does not consistently match the strongest classical baseline across seeds; however, the trained-DRU hybrid is the only model whose mean F1 macro shifts upward from full to strict (+0.05), a directional signal that the per-seed standard deviations prevent from being interpreted as a statistically established difference. The trained-DRU hybrid also records the lowest mean false-alarm rate under proxy-free evaluation, subject to the inter-seed variance reported. We frame this as an incremental, reproducible quantum-enhanced hybrid benefit, and provide an open Qiskit 2.x implementation as a benchmark for cybersecurity analytics in NISQ-era aerospace systems.
tldr: This paper applies quantum machine learning (data reuploading) to UAV anomaly detection, but does not address the user's core interests in information thermodynamics, quantum foundations, quantum communication, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To improve anomaly detection in UAVs using quantum machine learning while avoiding data leakage and evaluating the impact of proxy features.
method: A group-aware temporal protocol (B2) for dataset partitioning, a three-mode feature audit (full/loose/strict), and a hybrid XGBoost + Data Reuploading (DRU) classifier compared against classical baselines.
result: The trained-DRU hybrid shows a slight F1 macro improvement under strict proxy-free evaluation and the lowest false-alarm rate, but with high inter-seed variance preventing statistical significance.
conclusion: The hybrid approach offers incremental benefits, but the results are not statistically robust; the work provides an open Qiskit implementation for NISQ-era aerospace cybersecurity.

title: High-Rate Public-Key Pseudorandom Codes For Edit Errors
authors: Shengtang Huang, Xin Li, Songtao Mao, Zhaienhe Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pseudorandom codes (PRCs), introduced by Christ and Gunn (CRYPTO '2024), are error-correcting codes whose codewords are computationally indistinguishable from uniformly random strings, while still being decodable by someone holding the key. They provide a natural primitive for robust and undetectable watermarking, particularly in applications to AI-generated content. Although recent works have obtained strong results for substitution errors, the edit-error setting remains much less understood, especially in the high-rate regime and over small alphabets. We study public-key pseudorandom codes against edit errors. First, we give a new reduction showing that binary zero-bit PRCs robust against a constant fraction of substitution errors can be transformed into binary zero-bit PRCs robust against edit errors. Consequently, under any assumption that yields zero-bit Hamming-robust PRCs, one also obtains zero-bit PRCs for edit channels, albeit only for the weaker class of sublinear polynomial edit channels, namely channels with edit error rate [MATH] for any constant [MATH]. In the high-rate regime, we construct public-key PRCs with rate arbitrarily close to [MATH] over sufficiently large constant alphabets, and with rate arbitrarily close to [MATH] over the binary alphabet. Moreover, if we allow the alphabet size to be [MATH], where [MATH] is the security parameter, then our public-key PRCs can attain the Singleton bound for insertion-deletion channels. Taken together, these results yield the first high-rate public-key binary PRC constructions for edit channels, under the same assumption that yields zero-bit Hamming-robust PRCs.
tldr: This paper constructs high-rate public-key pseudorandom codes robust against edit errors, achieving rates close to 1 over large alphabets and 1/2 over binary alphabets.
motivation: Pseudorandom codes are useful for watermarking AI-generated content, but existing constructions for edit errors were limited, especially in the high-rate regime and over small alphabets.
method: The authors provide a reduction from substitution-robust PRCs to edit-robust PRCs for binary zero-bit codes, and construct explicit public-key PRCs using algebraic coding techniques and cryptographic assumptions.
result: They obtain binary zero-bit PRCs for edit channels with sublinear polynomial error rates, and high-rate public-key PRCs over large alphabets (rate arbitrarily close to 1) and binary alphabets (rate arbitrarily close to 1/2), with some constructions achieving the Singleton bound.
conclusion: These results provide the first high-rate public-key binary PRC constructions for edit channels, advancing the theory of pseudorandom codes and their applications to watermarking.

title: Ab Initio Simulation Of Market Dynamics
authors: Robert S. Farr
abstract: ArXiv:2605.18756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide simple models for the utility function (or psychology) of an actor trading a multitude of goods for money. In this framework, money has no intrinsic consumption value, but is required as a medium of exchange. A collection of such actors are then simulated interacting through market rules which create a double auction for each of the goods. This framework captures the self-consistent, rational behavior of independent actors, including how they make compromises between purchases of different goods; so goes beyond price-demand curves, and also generates the small-scale fluctuations from individual trades. We find that stable price formation requires a model that includes time-preference for the actors. Fluctuations in prices show a distribution with algebraic tails. Including inflation expectations leads to complex, damped or un-damped price oscillations. We attempt to model the dynamics of input-output economic models, but find it difficult to keep prices stable with the assumptions employed.
tldr: This paper models market dynamics using agent-based simulations with utility functions and double auctions, focusing on price formation and fluctuations.
motivation: To understand price formation and fluctuations in markets from first principles, going beyond simple supply-demand curves.
method: Agent-based simulation with actors having utility functions, trading goods for money via double auctions, including time preference and inflation expectations.
result: Stable prices require time preference; price fluctuations show algebraic tails; inflation expectations cause complex oscillations; input-output models are difficult to stabilize.
conclusion: The framework captures rational behavior and small-scale fluctuations, but stabilizing input-output models remains challenging.

title: Stop Drawing Scientific Claims From Llm Social Simulations Without Robustness Audits
authors: Jinyi Ye, Lei Cao, Ding Chen, Emilio Ferrara
abstract: ArXiv:2605.18890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scientific claims drawn from LLM social simulations should be no stronger than the robustness audits that support them. Generative agents bring new expressive power to agent-based modeling, enabling simulations of collective social processes like cooperation, polarization, and norm formation. Yet they also introduce complexity through additional architectural choices, such as agent specification, memory representation, interaction protocols, and environment design. Small perturbations that appear minor to researchers can cascade into macro-level outcomes through repeated interaction, creating a "butterfly effect." Consequently, scientific claims drawn from LLM social simulations may reflect implementation artifacts rather than the social mechanisms being modeled. We support this position with two case studies: a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma and a social media echo chamber simulation. Across multiple models, minor perturbations in persona format and game-instruction framing shift cooperation rates by up to 76 percentage points, while network homophily and hub assignment produce significant and consistent shifts in polarization metrics. We also find that sensitivity is unevenly distributed across both architectural choices and model families: the same perturbation that produces the 76 pp shift in one frontier model only shifts another by 1 pp. Robustness is therefore a property that should be measured per claim and per model, not assumed. To address this validation gap, we introduce TRAILS (Taxonomy for Robustness Audits In LLM Simulations), a robustness-audit taxonomy spanning three levels of simulation design: agent (micro-level), interaction (meso-level), and system (macro-level). We call for robustness to become a first-order validation requirement before LLM social simulations are used to explain mechanisms, evaluate interventions, or inform decisions.
tldr: This paper argues that scientific claims from LLM social simulations require robustness audits, demonstrating high sensitivity to minor design perturbations.
motivation: LLM-based social simulations are increasingly used to study collective behavior, but their sensitivity to architectural choices may produce artifacts rather than valid social mechanisms.
method: The authors conduct two case studies (repeated Prisoner's Dilemma and social media echo chamber) with multiple LLMs, varying persona formats, game instructions, network homophily, and hub assignments to measure outcome sensitivity.
result: Minor perturbations cause cooperation rate shifts up to 76 percentage points and significant polarization changes; sensitivity varies across models and design choices.
conclusion: Robustness must be a first-order validation requirement; the TRAILS taxonomy is proposed to standardize robustness audits across agent, interaction, and system levels.

title: Semiclassical Periodic-orbit Theory For Quantum Spectra
authors: Martin Sieber Sebastian M\"uller
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gutzwiller's trace formula has a central place in quantum chaos because it provides semiclassical approximations for quantum energy levels in classically chaotic systems by linking them to classical periodic orbits. In this didactic article, we discuss a derivation of the trace formula starting from the Feynman path integral. We then describe how the trace formula is used to explain universal features in the distribution of the quantum energy levels that are described by random matrix theory, and we give an overview of related work.
tldr: This paper reviews Gutzwiller's trace formula and its application to quantum chaos, linking classical periodic orbits to quantum energy levels.
motivation: To provide a didactic derivation of the trace formula and explain its role in understanding universal spectral statistics in chaotic systems.
method: Derivation from Feynman path integral and comparison with random matrix theory predictions.
result: The trace formula successfully reproduces random matrix theory statistics for chaotic systems.
conclusion: The work reinforces the semiclassical explanation of quantum chaos and suggests further studies in spectral correlations.

title: First-passage Processes In A Deterministic One-dimensional Cellular Automaton Model Of Traffic Flow
authors: Ofer Biham, Gilad Hertzberg Rabinovich, Eytan Katzav
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present analytical results for first-passage processes in a deterministic one-dimensional cellular automaton (CA) model of traffic flow. Starting at time [MATH] from a random initial state with car density p, at every time step [MATH] each car moves one step to the right if the cell on its right is empty, and is stopped if it is occupied by another car. The model, which coincides with CA rule 184 in Wolfram's numbering scheme, exhibits a continuous dynamical phase transition at [MATH], between a low-density free-flowing phase and a high-density congested phase. Using the framework of first-passage processes, we derive a closed-form expression for the distribution [MATH] of first-stopping (FS) times, which is the probability that a randomly selected car will be stopped for the first time at time [MATH]. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the stopping probability [MATH], which is the probability that a randomly selected car will be stopped at time [MATH]. In the low-density phase of [MATH], the probability [MATH] yields a closed-form expression for the distribution [MATH] of last-stopping (LS) times, which is the probability that a randomly selected car will be stopped for the last time at time [MATH], beyond which it will move freely indefinitely. In this regime, we analyze the relation between the LS time and the number of stopping events [MATH] which take place up to that time. We present closed-form expressions for the joint distribution [MATH], for the two conditional distributions that emanate from it and for the marginal distribution [MATH]. These results provide insight on the time scales of congestion and relaxation in deterministic traffic flow from the point of view of individual cars. In a broader context, they provide insight on complex relaxation processes that involve many interacting particles, such as deterministic surface growth.
tldr: This paper analytically solves first-passage processes in a deterministic cellular automaton model of traffic flow, deriving distributions of stopping times.
motivation: To understand time scales of congestion and relaxation in deterministic traffic flow from the perspective of individual cars, and to provide insight into complex relaxation processes in interacting particle systems.
method: Using the framework of first-passage processes on a one-dimensional deterministic cellular automaton (CA rule 184) with random initial conditions, deriving closed-form expressions for first-stopping and last-stopping time distributions.
result: Closed-form expressions for the distribution of first-stopping times, stopping probability, and last-stopping times in the low-density phase, along with joint and conditional distributions relating last-stopping time to number of stopping events.
conclusion: The results provide analytical insight into congestion dynamics in traffic flow and may inform understanding of relaxation processes in other deterministic many-particle systems, such as surface growth.

title: Tunable Cylindrical Vector Beam Generation Via Low-cost Printed Binary Holograms
authors: Emilio E. Ramos-Torres, Beatriz Morales Cruzado, Benjamin Perez-Garcia, Carmelo Rosales-Guzm\'an
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a low-cost method for generating cylindrical vector beams using binary holograms printed on acetate sheets and a modified Michelson interferometer incorporating a cylindrical-lens mode converter. By simply exchanging the hologram the device produces a variety of CVBs with tunable spatial-polarisation nonseparability. The transverse polarisation distributions reconstructed via Stokes polarimetry show spatial-polarisation features consistent with numerical simulations. The degree of nonseparability is further quantified using the vector quality factor (concurrence), demonstrating values in good agreement with theoretical expectations across the generated states. The use of wave-plate retarders enables continuous tuning from scalar to fully vector beams. The simplicity, robustness, and low cost of the proposed system make it an attractive alternative to programmable modulators for compact optical platforms and teaching laboratories.
tldr: A low-cost method for generating cylindrical vector beams using printed binary holograms and a modified Michelson interferometer is demonstrated.
motivation: To provide a simple, robust, and inexpensive alternative to programmable spatial light modulators for generating cylindrical vector beams, suitable for compact optical platforms and teaching.
method: Binary holograms printed on acetate sheets are used in a modified Michelson interferometer with a cylindrical-lens mode converter; Stokes polarimetry reconstructs transverse polarization distributions.
result: The device produces tunable cylindrical vector beams with spatial-polarization nonseparability; the vector quality factor (concurrence) matches theoretical predictions, and wave-plate retarders enable continuous tuning from scalar to fully vector beams.
conclusion: The system offers a low-cost, robust alternative for generating cylindrical vector beams, with potential applications in education and compact optical setups.

title: On The Single Field Formulation In Magnetostatics
authors: Giuseppe Tomassetti Stefan Kr\"omer
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We systematically discuss the equivalence of two variational formulations of magnetostatics, in terms of magnetization and magnetic field on the one hand and the single field formulation using only magnetic induction. To demonstrate that this link is stable also when the magnetic laws are coupled with other variational static models, elasticity is included in the models as well. Interestingly, despite the fact that the corresponding magnetoelastic energy densities in the material can be computed via Legendre-Fenchel transform in the magnetic state variables, the two formulations are not linked by standard convex duality on the level of the functionals. In addition, convexity and coercivity of the given functional are neither required for the transformation nor always preserved by it.
tldr: This paper discusses the equivalence of two variational formulations of magnetostatics, focusing on the single field formulation using magnetic induction and its coupling with elasticity, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum communication.
motivation: To systematically clarify the relationship between two variational formulations of magnetostatics and to demonstrate that this link remains stable when coupled with elasticity.
method: The authors compare the magnetization-magnetic field formulation with the single field formulation using magnetic induction, and include elasticity to test the stability of the equivalence. They use Legendre-Fenchel transforms and analyze convexity and coercivity conditions.
result: The two formulations are not linked by standard convex duality at the functional level, and convexity/coercivity are neither required nor preserved by the transformation.
conclusion: The findings have implications for modeling magnetoelastic materials, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is presented.

title: High-stability Offset-frequency Locking Of Two Lasers Using A Balanced Filter Discriminator
authors: Sang Eon Park, Meung Ho Seo, Young-Ho Park, Hyun-Gue Hong, Sang-Bum Lee, Sangwon Seo, Jae Hoon Lee, Seji Kang, Taeg Yong Kwon
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a high-stability laser offset-frequency locking technique based on a balanced filter discriminator. The beat note between two 852 nm external-cavity diode lasers is down-converted in two parallel arms using local-oscillator frequencies placed symmetrically around the desired offset frequency. After low-pass filtering and RMS detection, differential subtraction of the two detector outputs produces a dispersive frequency-error signal with a zero crossing primarily defined by the reference local-oscillator frequencies. This balanced configuration reduces sensitivity to common beat-power fluctuations and can improve the effective error-signal signal-to-noise ratio. The system was implemented for an 8.653 GHz offset corresponding to the cesium repumping frequency difference used in our laser-cooling setup. Measurements with different low-pass filters reveal a trade-off between discrimination sensitivity and feedback bandwidth. With an SLP-1.9+ filter, the locked beat frequency reached a fractional instability of [MATH] at 10 s when referred to the 852 nm optical carrier. The residual dependence on photodetector optical power was also characterized, showing that amplitude-to-frequency conversion remains small in the optimized differential configuration. This approach provides a practical frequency-only offset-locking method for atomic-physics experiments requiring stable and tunable microwave-scale laser frequency offsets.
tldr: This paper presents a laser offset-frequency locking technique using a balanced filter discriminator for stable microwave-scale frequency offsets, applied to cesium repumping in laser cooling.
motivation: To achieve high-stability offset-frequency locking between two lasers for atomic physics experiments, specifically for cesium repumping in laser cooling setups.
method: The beat note between two 852 nm lasers is down-converted using two local oscillators symmetrically placed around the desired offset, then low-pass filtered and RMS detected; differential subtraction yields a dispersive error signal.
result: The locked beat frequency achieved fractional instability of 10^-12 at 10 s, with low sensitivity to optical power fluctuations; trade-off between sensitivity and bandwidth was characterized.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical, frequency-only offset-locking method for stable and tunable microwave-scale offsets, useful for atomic physics experiments.

title: Unbiased Gradients For A Class Of Conditional Stochastic Optimization Problems
authors: Ajay Jasra Miguel Alvarez
abstract: ArXiv:2605.18786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider the conditional stochastic optimization (CSO) problem. This consists of optimizing a function which can be written as the expectation of a function which is itself a function of a conditional expectation, i.e.~of the type [MATH], where precise definitions are given in the main text. We address a particular class of CSO problems where the joint law of the random variables [MATH] cannot be exactly sampled; this case has been addressed in Goda & Kitade (2023). We introduce a method that combines Markovian stochastic approximation with unbiased approximation methods which allows one to find the optimizer of [MATH] in the context of interest. We illustrate our methodology on two examples associated to parameter estimation with model averaging and portfolio selection associated to high-dimensional full factor multivariate stochastic volatility models.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for unbiased gradient estimation in conditional stochastic optimization problems where the joint distribution cannot be exactly sampled.
motivation: To address a class of conditional stochastic optimization problems where exact sampling from the joint distribution is infeasible, extending prior work by Goda & Kitade.
method: Combines Markovian stochastic approximation with unbiased approximation methods to estimate gradients and find the optimizer.
result: The methodology is illustrated on parameter estimation with model averaging and portfolio selection using high-dimensional multivariate stochastic volatility models.
conclusion: The approach provides a way to handle CSO problems with inaccessible joint distributions, with potential applications in finance and statistics.

title: The Extremum Stack Is A Minimal Sufficient Statistic For Rate-Independent Functionals: A Kolmogorov Complexity Characterisation
authors: Piotr Frydrych
abstract: ArXiv:2605.18885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the extremum stack of a discrete sequence is a minimal sufficient statistic for the class of all computable, causal, rate-independent functionals, in the sense of Kolmogorov complexity. Specifically, we establish K(Pi_n) - O(1) <= K_R(u_{0:n}) <= K(Pi_n) + O(1), where K_R(u_{0:n}) is the length of the shortest program answering every query in the class R, and the O(1) overhead is independent of both the sequence length n and the stack depth k. Sufficiency follows from the classical wiping property of the Preisach hysteresis operator. Minimality is established via a finite indicator family whose rate-independence is verified explicitly. Any compression of a hysteresis-driven stream that preserves the full class R must therefore retain at least K(Pi_n) - O(1) bits; the stack-based compression algorithm implied by the result carries a Kolmogorov optimality guarantee that none of the standard time-series compression methods provide.
tldr: This paper proves that the extremum stack is a minimal sufficient statistic for rate-independent functionals using Kolmogorov complexity, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To characterize the minimal information needed to predict outputs of rate-independent systems, motivated by hysteresis modeling.
method: Uses Kolmogorov complexity and the Preisach hysteresis operator to establish sufficiency and minimality of the extremum stack.
result: The extremum stack is shown to be a minimal sufficient statistic for computable, causal, rate-independent functionals, with Kolmogorov complexity bounds.
conclusion: The stack-based compression is optimal for rate-independent streams, but the work is purely theoretical and unrelated to quantum systems.

title: Scalable Iterative Gramian Synthesis For Control-affine Systems
authors: Zongxi Yu, Cyprien Tamekue, Ruiqi Chen, Shinung Ching
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents a scalable implementation of nonlinear Gramian-based control synthesis for control-affine systems, including a minimum energy control construction. These synthesis advances are achieved by addressing key computational bottlenecks inherent to iterative synthesis map formulations, yielding a computational scheme that exhibits rapid convergence and high-precision. The efficacy of this synthesis framework is demonstrated across five canonical nonlinear control systems and 100-dimensional recurrent neural network models, including underactuated systems. Empirical scaling results further indicate that convergence is primarily governed by intrinsic system properties, such as nonlinearity and controllability, rather than by state-space dimensionality. This work provides a practical, scalable computational pathway for translating rigorous nonlinear synthesis theory into high-dimensional control applications.
tldr: This paper presents a scalable numerical method for nonlinear control synthesis using Gramians, applied to high-dimensional systems like RNNs.
motivation: To overcome computational bottlenecks in iterative Gramian-based control synthesis for high-dimensional control-affine systems.
method: Develops a scalable iterative algorithm that computes controllability and observability Gramians for nonlinear control-affine systems, with a minimum energy control construction.
result: Demonstrates rapid convergence and high precision on five canonical nonlinear systems and 100-dimensional RNNs; convergence depends on intrinsic system properties rather than dimensionality.
conclusion: Provides a practical pathway for applying nonlinear control theory to high-dimensional systems, with potential for broader use in machine learning and robotics.

title: Recovering Complex Unitary Eigenspaces From Real-Valued Embeddings
authors: N. Anders Petersson Stefanie G\"unther
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of recovering a unitary eigendecomposition of a complex unitary matrix from that of its embedded real-valued formulation. Such formulations arise naturally in scientific computing workflows that employ real-arithmetic solvers by representing complex matrices in term of their real and imaginary parts. While the reconstruction is trivial when the spectrum of the real-valued embedding is simple, degenerate and/or complex conjugated eigenvalues introduce ambiguities because each eigenspace may include contributions from both the unitary matrix and its complex conjugate. We prove that this ambiguity can always be resolved by applying a structured projection to the eigenspaces of the real-valued embedding, followed by a rank-revealing orthonormalization. The resulting procedure recovers the eigenvalues and an unitary eigenbasis for the original unitary matrix, with correct multiplicities of degenerate eigenvalues.
tldr: This paper presents a method to recover the unitary eigendecomposition of a complex unitary matrix from the eigendecomposition of its real-valued embedding, handling degenerate and complex conjugate eigenvalues.
motivation: In scientific computing, complex matrices are often represented as real-valued embeddings to use real-arithmetic solvers, but recovering the original complex eigendecomposition is nontrivial when eigenvalues are degenerate or appear in complex conjugate pairs.
method: The authors prove that the ambiguity can be resolved by applying a structured projection to the eigenspaces of the real-valued embedding, followed by a rank-revealing orthonormalization.
result: The procedure recovers the eigenvalues and a unitary eigenbasis for the original unitary matrix, correctly handling degenerate eigenvalues and their multiplicities.
conclusion: This work provides a rigorous solution to a numerical linear algebra problem, with potential applications in scientific computing workflows that use real-arithmetic solvers for complex matrices.

title: Mode-Tensorized Canonical Polyadic Decomposition For Mimo Channel Estimation
authors: Alexander Blagodarnyi, Alexander Sherstobitov, Vladimir Lyashev
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a channel estimation method for Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems based on Canonical Polyadic (CP) decomposition applied to a mode-factorized tensor representation of the channel. The proposed approach reshapes the original low-order channel tensor into a higher-order tensor by factorizing its modes into multiple virtual modes, thereby introducing additional dimensions. By exploiting the sparse structure of MIMO channels and the plane-wave propagation model in the far-field regime, the proposed mode tensorization enhances the separability of individual propagation paths. It is shown that increasing the number of tensor modes improves component separation and provides inherent denoising effects. Building on these properties, a mode-tensorized CP decomposition (MTCPD) algorithm is developed. In addition, a metric for analyzing the virtual factors obtained from MTCPD is proposed, enabling estimation of the canonical rank and selection of the most informative components contributing to overall system performance. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method improves channel estimation accuracy compared to conventional tensor-based approaches, particularly under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.
tldr: This paper proposes a mode-tensorized CP decomposition method for MIMO channel estimation, focusing on improving accuracy under low SNR.
motivation: To enhance channel estimation accuracy in MIMO systems by exploiting tensor decomposition and mode factorization.
method: The channel tensor is reshaped into a higher-order tensor by factorizing modes into virtual modes, then CP decomposition is applied to separate propagation paths.
result: The method improves channel estimation accuracy, especially under low SNR, and provides a metric for rank estimation and component selection.
conclusion: The approach offers better denoising and component separation, with potential for practical MIMO systems.

title: Sharp Analysis Of Sketched Least Squares And Randomized Low-rank Approximation
authors: Robert J. Webber Ethan N. Epperly
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two widely used randomized algorithms are the sketch-and-solve method for least-squares regression and the randomized SVD for low-rank approximation. These algorithms apply a random embedding to compress a target matrix, and they perform computations on the compressed matrix to save computational cost. This paper asks, what is the optimal random embedding in these algorithms? Also, what is the sharpest possible error bound for the optimal embedding? The paper proves that a random orthonormal matrix is minimax optimal for the sketch-and-solve algorithm while any rotation-invariant embedding is minimax optimal for the randomized SVD. Following these results, the paper obtains the best possible error bounds for sketched least-squares and the randomized SVD. Last, empirical experiments provide evidence of universality phenomena, in which several random embeddings lead to similar accuracy to the optimal embeddings in practice.
tldr: This paper analyzes optimal random embeddings for sketched least-squares and randomized SVD, proving minimax optimality of random orthonormal matrices and rotation-invariant embeddings.
motivation: To determine the optimal random embedding and sharpest error bounds for two widely used randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra.
method: Theoretical analysis using minimax optimality criteria and empirical experiments comparing various random embeddings.
result: Random orthonormal matrices are minimax optimal for sketch-and-solve; any rotation-invariant embedding is minimax optimal for randomized SVD. Sharp error bounds are derived.
conclusion: The findings provide theoretical guidance for choosing embeddings in practice and suggest universality phenomena where many embeddings perform similarly.

title: Correcting Tail Deletions In Rank Modulated Composite Encoding For Data Storage In Dna
authors: Tomer Cohen, Eitan Yaakobi, Zohar Yakhini
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the combination of two recent coding approaches, in the context of DNA based data storage. Composite DNA alphabets leverage properties of the DNA synthesis and sequencing process. A composite symbol does not represent a single nucleotide, but rather a designed mixture of DNA nucleotides. Using the high multiplicity that is intrinsic to synthesis and sequencing a composite symbol consists of frequencies in the mixture. Rank modulation codes use permutations to represent information. Combining the two, we construct encoding that uses permutations of nucleotide frequencies rather than the exact frequency values. Codes for this approach were addressed in previous work, under Kendall's tau distances. In this work we study deletion and insertion codes. We present bounds and constructions of efficient codes defined over partial permutations.
tldr: This paper studies deletion and insertion error-correcting codes for rank-modulated composite DNA storage, focusing on partial permutations and Kendall tau distance.
motivation: DNA data storage requires robust coding schemes to handle errors from synthesis and sequencing. Composite DNA alphabets and rank modulation are promising but need deletion/insertion correction.
method: The authors derive bounds and construct efficient codes for correcting tail deletions in rank-modulated composite encoding, using combinatorial and coding-theoretic techniques.
result: New bounds and explicit code constructions for deletion/insertion errors in partial permutations are presented, improving on previous work limited to Kendall tau distance.
conclusion: The work advances error correction for DNA storage, but its focus on coding theory is tangential to the user's interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Inference Functionals And Observation Operators For Distributional Statistical Models
authors: R. Labouriau
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper generalises inference functions (Godambe, 1960) to distributional statistical models, in which each probability measure is represented by a distribution--kernel pair [MATH]. The generalisation is strategically motivated: the key properties of maximum likelihood estimation-consistency and asymptotic normality -derive not from maximising the likelihood but from the MLE being the root of a regular inference function. Extending inference functions to the distributional setting provides an optimality theory for models lacking classical densities or finite moments. The extension requires enlarging the notion of observation. We introduce observation operators [MATH] mapping distributional models to an observation space, and define inference functionals as estimating equations composed with these operators. The framework encompasses classical point observations, interval-censored data, convolutional measurements, and transform-based statistics. We establish asymptotic theory (consistency, asymptotic normality, Godambe optimality) under mild conditions and derive a hierarchy of information bounds -- classical Fisher information dominates the information available through the observation operator, which in turn dominates the information captured by any inference functional -- via the H\'ajek--Le~Cam convolution theorem. The two gaps quantify distinct sources of information loss: the observation mechanism and the choice of inference functional. Examples include sinusoidal inference functions for heavy-tailed distributions, interval-censored location inference, elliptically contoured models, and nuisance parameters via the Bhapkar--Godambe projection.
tldr: This paper generalizes inference functions to distributional statistical models, introducing observation operators and establishing asymptotic theory and information bounds.
motivation: To extend the theory of inference functions to settings where classical densities or finite moments are lacking, such as interval-censored data or heavy-tailed distributions.
method: The authors define inference functionals composed with observation operators, and derive asymptotic properties (consistency, normality, optimality) under mild conditions, using the Hájek–Le Cam convolution theorem.
result: A hierarchy of information bounds is established: classical Fisher information dominates observation-operator information, which dominates inference-functional information, quantifying two sources of information loss.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified optimality theory for distributional models and identifies gaps due to observation and inference choices, with potential applications in robust statistics and complex data types.

title: Domain-Adaptive Communication-Rate Optimization For Sim-to-Real Humanoid-Robot Wireless Xr Teleoperation
authors: Caolu Xu, Zhiyong Chen, Meixia Tao, Li Song, Feng Yang, Wenjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless extended reality (XR) teleoperation provides embodied interaction capability for collecting humanoid robot demonstrations, but the large-scale adoption is restricted by the overhead of high-frequency motion transmission. This paper develops a system framework that integrates sampling, transmission, interpolation, and reconstruction and formulates a communication-rate optimization that aims to minimize the communication energy while maintaining the reconstruction accuracy of robot motion trajectories through dimension-wise sampling-rate control. Since acquiring real-time feedback from physical robots is limited by hardware costs, it is necessary to solve the problem through simulator interaction with offline real-domain data correction. To guide sim-to-real adaptation, we provide a PAC-Bayes generalization characterization that reveals the effects of latent density-ratio estimation, finite-sample deviation, and encoder bias. Building on this analysis, we propose a proximal policy optimization (PPO) method with density-ratio weighting and trust-region regularization. Experiments on public humanoid teleoperation dataset show that the proposed method improves the tradeoff between reconstruction error and communication energy consumption under sim-to-real distribution shift. We further analyze the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm across various wireless channels and dynamic motion trajectories.
tldr: This paper optimizes communication rates for humanoid robot teleoperation using domain adaptation, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To reduce communication energy in wireless XR teleoperation while maintaining reconstruction accuracy, addressing sim-to-real distribution shifts.
method: Proposes a system framework with sampling, transmission, interpolation, and reconstruction, and uses PPO with density-ratio weighting and trust-region regularization guided by PAC-Bayes analysis.
result: The method improves the tradeoff between reconstruction error and communication energy under sim-to-real shifts, validated on a public humanoid teleoperation dataset.
conclusion: The approach effectively adapts to real-world distribution shifts, but the paper focuses on robotics and wireless communication, not quantum systems.

title: A Von Neumann-Jordan Constant Of Non-Normable Metrics
authors: Nguyen Duy Cuong Doan Huu Hieu
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper studies a generalized von Neumann-Jordan constant of non-normable metrics on vector spaces. To the best of our knowledge, all existing results of the von Neumann-Jordan constant and its generalizations have been established only in the normed setting. We identify reasonable conditions on non-normable metrics under which results known for norms remain valid. Several examples and counterexamples are provided to justify the established results. The computation for a class of non-normable metrics on product spaces is also investigated. In particular, we give precise formulas for the generalized von Neumann-Jordan constant of p-metrics under a metric-type Clarkson inequality. Comparisons with existing results are discussed throughout the paper whenever applicable.
tldr: This paper generalizes the von Neumann-Jordan constant to non-normable metric spaces, extending results from normed settings.
motivation: All existing results on the von Neumann-Jordan constant were limited to normed spaces; the authors aimed to extend these to non-normable metrics.
method: The study identifies conditions on non-normable metrics that allow known normed-space results to hold, and provides examples and counterexamples. It also computes the constant for p-metrics using a metric-type Clarkson inequality.
result: Reasonable conditions are found under which the generalized constant behaves similarly to the normed case, and explicit formulas are given for certain classes of metrics.
conclusion: The work opens up the study of geometric constants in non-normable settings, with potential applications in functional analysis and metric geometry.

title: Optimal Spectral Algorithms For Correlated Two-view Models In High Dimensions
authors: Hang Du, Henry Hu, Saba Lepsveridze
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study high-dimensional inference in correlated two-view models, focusing on spectral methods for strong detection and weak recovery. We introduce a general framework, motivated by a TAP type heuristic from statistical physics, that provides a unified treatment of three canonical models: high-dimensional canonical correlation analysis, and the correlated spiked Wigner and Wishart models. Our main contribution is to construct explicit spectral algorithms in all three settings, that achieve strong detection and weak recovery down to the corresponding thresholds, where we prove matching information-theoretic lower bounds. Furthermore, our spectral procedures operate without knowledge of the model parameters, relying solely on the observed data. This demonstrates the optimality of spectral methods in these models and the broad statistical applicability of the framework.
tldr: This paper develops optimal spectral algorithms for high-dimensional inference in correlated two-view models, focusing on detection and recovery thresholds.
motivation: To provide a unified framework and optimal spectral methods for three canonical high-dimensional models, motivated by statistical physics heuristics.
method: The authors introduce a TAP-type heuristic from statistical physics to construct spectral algorithms that achieve strong detection and weak recovery down to information-theoretic thresholds, without knowledge of model parameters.
result: Explicit spectral algorithms are shown to be optimal for correlated spiked Wigner, Wishart, and CCA models, with matching lower bounds.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the optimality of spectral methods in these models and suggests broad applicability of the framework to other high-dimensional inference problems.

title: Convergence Of Iterates And Improved Rates For Accelerated Augmented Lagrangian Methods For Linearly Constrained Convex Optimization
authors: Xin He, Nan-Jing Hang, Yi-Bin Xiao, Ya-Ping Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a linearly constrained convex optimization problem with a differentiable objective function. Motivated by an inertial primal-dual dynamical system with vanishing damping, we propose a class of accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods with Nesterov extrapolation parameters. The framework contains two variants: an implicit-gradient scheme for convex continuously differentiable objectives and a partially explicit scheme for convex smooth objectives. Under suitable parameter conditions, we prove convergence of the primal-dual sequence to a saddle point, together with accelerated estimates for the augmented Lagrangian gap, the feasibility violation, and the objective residual. In the noncritical parameter regime, these estimates are improved from [MATH] to [MATH]. To the best of our knowledge, such little-o rates for both feasibility violation and objective residual have not been previously established for accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods in this setting.
tldr: This paper proposes accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods for linearly constrained convex optimization, proving convergence and improved rates.
motivation: To develop faster optimization algorithms for convex problems with linear constraints, motivated by inertial primal-dual dynamical systems.
method: The authors propose two variants of accelerated augmented Lagrangian methods using Nesterov extrapolation parameters: an implicit-gradient scheme for general convex objectives and a partially explicit scheme for smooth objectives.
result: Convergence of the primal-dual sequence to a saddle point is proved, with accelerated little-o rates for feasibility violation and objective residual that improve upon previous results.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical advances in optimization algorithms, with potential applications in large-scale convex optimization, but is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Worst-Case Utility Privacy Mechanism Via Pointwise Maximal Leakage
authors: Tobias J. Oechtering Ci Song
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a discrete privacy mechanism exploiting beneficial properties of the novel privacy measure Pointwise Maximal Leakage (PML). Given the utility assignment characterized by every input-output letter pair, we study the mechanism design problem that satisfies PML privacy guarantees and maximizes the worst-case utility. Unlike popular privacy measures like Differential Privacy (DP), PML allows us to set some conditional probabilities in the mechanism to be zero and thereby preventing the occurrence of some low utilities while preserving a strict PML constraint. We show that the utility-safe mechanism, with low computational complexity, is optimal for the worst-case utility problem with an additional constraint on the output support set. We finally demonstrate the effectiveness in several numerical experiments. Due to DP's inability to have zeros in the mechanism, the design of privacy mechanisms that optimize the worst-case utility is underexplored, and this work shows that PML is a privacy measure that is perfectly suited for this purpose.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy mechanism using Pointwise Maximal Leakage to maximize worst-case utility, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To design privacy mechanisms that optimize worst-case utility, which is underexplored due to limitations of Differential Privacy.
method: Formulates a mechanism design problem with PML constraints and an output support set constraint, solved with low computational complexity.
result: The proposed utility-safe mechanism is optimal for worst-case utility under PML, allowing zero conditional probabilities to avoid low utilities.
conclusion: PML is well-suited for worst-case utility privacy mechanisms, demonstrated via numerical experiments.

title: Breaking Of Invariant Curves: From The Fermi-Ulam Map To The Breathing Circle Billiard
authors: Stefano Mar\`o Jos\'e Lamas
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the breathing circle billiard, in which a point particle moves freely inside a disk. The radius varies periodically in time, with elastic reflections at the moving boundary. In this system the angular momentum is preserved, and fixing its value [MATH] reduces the dynamics to a two-dimensional exact symplectic map on a cylinder. In the high-energy regime this map is a twist map generated by a diagonally periodic generating function [MATH]. We study the small angular momentum regime as a perturbation of the limiting case [MATH], which corresponds to the Fermi-Ulam dynamics along a diameter. Using this perturbative structure and a quantitative version of Mather's converse-KAM criterion, we exclude invariant Lipschitz graphs for suitable rotation numbers. Combined with Aubry-Mather theory and Forni's theorem, this yields positive topological entropy for sufficiently small [MATH]. Our result improves previous similar results obtained via the standard Mather's converse-KAM criterion by giving a sharper quantitative threshold for the destruction of invariant curves.
tldr: This paper studies the destruction of invariant curves in a breathing circle billiard using converse-KAM theory and Aubry-Mather theory.
motivation: To understand the transition from integrability to chaos in time-dependent billiard systems, specifically the breathing circle billiard, and to improve quantitative thresholds for the breakdown of invariant curves.
method: The authors reduce the dynamics to a two-dimensional symplectic map, treat small angular momentum as a perturbation of the Fermi-Ulam map, and apply a quantitative version of Mather's converse-KAM criterion combined with Aubry-Mather theory and Forni's theorem.
result: They obtain a sharper quantitative threshold for the destruction of invariant curves and prove positive topological entropy for sufficiently small angular momentum.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of Hamiltonian chaos in time-dependent billiards and provides improved criteria for non-existence of invariant tori.

title: A Spline-based Physics-Informed Numerical Scheme: Accurate Smooth Solutions For Differential Equations
authors: Fatima Mroue Ayman Mourad
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rise of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) has popularized the concept of solving differential equations via residual minimization. However, neural networks are often viewed as ``black boxes" requiring significant computational overhead and stochastic optimization. Moreover, PINNs typically treat boundary conditions (BCs) as ``soft constraints" within the loss function and this makes the optimization process struggling to enforce the BCs properly. This paper introduces the , a numerical framework designed to solve both initial and boundary value problems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). By replacing the neural network architecture of traditional PINNs with a structured spline basis, SPINS achieves high accuracy and interpretability with a minimal parameter set. In addition, the BCs are automatically satisfied from the choice of the splines architecture. Therefore, SPINS provides smooth numerical solutions for ODEs allowing analytical differentiation. Moreover, SPINS benefits from the automatic differentiation where computing the gradient of the physics-informed loss function is an easy task making the optimization process very fast using gradient-based optimizers such as the L-BFGS-B algorithm. We demonstrate the efficacy of SPINS on nonlinear second order ODEs with several choices of BCs using cubic and quintic interpolating splines and present its natural extension to high order ODEs.
tldr: This paper introduces SPINS, a spline-based numerical framework for solving ODEs that replaces neural networks in PINNs to achieve high accuracy and interpretability.
motivation: To overcome the black-box nature, computational overhead, and difficulty in enforcing boundary conditions in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs).
method: Replaces neural network architecture with a structured spline basis (cubic and quintic interpolating splines) that automatically satisfies boundary conditions, and uses automatic differentiation with gradient-based optimization (L-BFGS-B).
result: SPINS achieves accurate smooth solutions for nonlinear second-order ODEs with various boundary conditions, and extends naturally to higher-order ODEs.
conclusion: SPINS offers a fast, interpretable, and accurate alternative to PINNs for solving ODEs, with potential for extension to PDEs and other applications.

title: GLOBe: A Modular Global Optimization Library
authors: Ga\"etan Serr\'e (ENS Paris Saclay, CB), Argyris Kalogeratos (CB, ENS Paris Saclay), Nicolas Vayatis
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-source libraries are have a catalytic role in research pipelines, where new methods must be compared against up-to-date baselines. We present the GLobal Optimization Benchmark (GLOBe) modular Python library that unifies classical and recent continuous global optimization algorithms, including decision-based and mathematically founded particle-based methods, in a single framework. A central contribution of GLOBe is its modular architecture, which factors common algorithmic patterns into reusable familyl evel components and enables plugins to be implemented once and makes them available to all algorithms in the corresponding family. This modular design leverages recent advances in mathematical formalization of global optimization, where structural commonalities across algorithms have been identified and used to develop broadly applicable, formally grounded algorithmic features. The C++ backend relies on Eigen 5 for efficient linear algebra. GLOBe presently includes 14 optimizers, 19 analytical benchmarks along with a random function generator, and an integrated toolkit for direct algorithm comparison.
tldr: GLOBe is a modular Python library for continuous global optimization, unifying classical and recent algorithms with a reusable component architecture.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date, modular benchmarking framework for global optimization algorithms, facilitating fair comparison and reuse of algorithmic components.
method: The library implements a modular architecture that factors common algorithmic patterns into family-level components, with a C++ backend using Eigen for efficiency. It includes 14 optimizers, 19 benchmarks, and a random function generator.
result: GLOBe offers a unified, extensible platform for global optimization research, enabling easy integration of new algorithms and comparison against baselines.
conclusion: The library aims to accelerate research in global optimization by reducing implementation overhead and promoting reproducible benchmarking.

title: Influence As Soft Sparsity: Estimation Of Monotone Functions On $\{0,1\}^d$
authors: G\'erard Biau
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of estimating a monotone function [MATH] from noisy observations at uniformly random vertices of the Boolean hypercube. As a measure of complexity for the target~[MATH], we use the total [MATH]-influence [MATH], a classical quantity in Boolean analysis that is nonnegative for monotone functions and controls the effective dimensionality of the estimation problem: through a spectral concentration result in the spirit of Friedgut's junta theorem, the Fourier spectrum of any [MATH] with [MATH] concentrates on low-degree subsets of the influential coordinates. We establish minimax bounds over the class [MATH]: \[ c\,{(\log n)^{3/2}} \;\leqslant\; \inf\_{\hat f}\;\sup\_{f\in\cF\_K}\; \E\bigl[\|\hat f - f\|\_2^2\bigr] \;\leqslant\; C\,{}, \] where [MATH] is the sample size. The upper bound holds for all [MATH] and is uniform in the ambient dimension~[MATH] (under the mild condition [MATH]). It is achieved by a Fourier thresholding estimator that adapts to the unknown~[MATH]. The lower bound relies on a Varshamov--Gilbert packing on the middle layer of the hypercube combined with Fano's inequality.
tldr: This paper studies minimax optimal estimation of monotone functions on the Boolean hypercube using total influence as a complexity measure.
motivation: To understand how the complexity of monotone functions, measured by total influence, affects the sample complexity of estimation from noisy observations.
method: The paper uses Fourier analysis on the Boolean hypercube, a spectral concentration result akin to Friedgut's junta theorem, and a Fourier thresholding estimator that adapts to unknown influence. Lower bounds are derived via Varshamov–Gilbert packing and Fano's inequality.
result: Minimax bounds are established: the minimax risk is between c (log n)^{3/2} and C, where n is sample size, with the upper bound uniform in ambient dimension d.
conclusion: The work provides a tight characterization of estimation complexity for monotone functions under influence constraints, with implications for high-dimensional statistics and Boolean function analysis.

title: Convergence Of Consensus-Based Particle Methods For Nonconvex Bi-Level Optimization
authors: Yutong Chao, Xudong Sun, Konstantin Riedl, Majid Khadiv, Jalal Etesami
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a consensus-based optimization method for nonconvex bi-level optimization, where the objective is to minimize an upper-level function over the set of global minimizers of a lower-level problem. The proposed approach is derivative-free, and constructs its consensus point via smooth quantile selection combined with a Gibbs-type Laplace approximation. We establish convergence guarantees for both the associated dynamics and its approximation. In particular, under suitable assumptions on smooth quantile localization, error bounds, and stability, we show that the mean-field law reaches any arbitrary prescribed Wasserstein neighborhood of the target bi-level solution with an explicit exponential rate up to the hitting time. Numerical experiments on a two-dimensional constrained problem and neural network training further support the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper proposes a consensus-based derivative-free optimization method for nonconvex bi-level problems with convergence guarantees.
motivation: Bi-level optimization is challenging, especially when the lower-level problem is nonconvex and derivative information is unavailable.
method: The method uses smooth quantile selection and Gibbs-type Laplace approximation to construct consensus points, and analyzes mean-field dynamics.
result: The mean-field law converges to the target bi-level solution with exponential rate up to a hitting time, supported by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The approach offers a derivative-free solution for nonconvex bi-level optimization, with potential applications in hyperparameter tuning and meta-learning.

title: Reduction And Inverse-reduction Functors I: Standard $\mathsf{V^k}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-modules
authors: Justine Fasquel, Ethan Fursman, David Ridout
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum hamiltonian reduction is a fundamental tool of conformal field theory and vertex algebra representation theory. It has traditionally been applied to study highest-weight modules. On the other hand, inverse quantum hamiltonian reduction lends itself to the study of fully relaxed highest-weight modules and their spectral flows, sometimes called the standard modules. This is the first of several papers that study the composition of reduction and inverse-reduction functors. A general formalism is presented and exemplified with the simplest example, thereby computing the action of reduction on the standard modules of the affine vertex-operator algebra associated with [MATH]. The appearence of unbounded spectral sequences in this formalism may be of independent interest.
tldr: This paper develops a formalism for composing reduction and inverse-reduction functors in vertex algebra representation theory, applied to standard modules of affine sl(2) vertex-operator algebras.
motivation: To understand the composition of quantum Hamiltonian reduction and its inverse, which are important tools in conformal field theory and vertex algebra representation theory, particularly for studying standard modules.
method: The authors present a general formalism for composing reduction and inverse-reduction functors, and illustrate it with the simplest example of affine sl(2) vertex-operator algebras, using spectral sequences.
result: The action of reduction on standard modules is computed, and unbounded spectral sequences appear, which may be of independent interest.
conclusion: This work lays the foundation for further studies of reduction and inverse-reduction functors, with potential applications to more complex vertex algebras and conformal field theories.

title: Feedback Stabilization Of Switched Systems: Memory Is Not Needed
authors: Thiago Alves Lima (ITA), Matteo Della Rossa (polito), Antoine Girard
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A long-standing assumption in the literature on switched linear systems is that static, homogeneous of degree one feedbacks form the most general class of controllers necessary and sufficient for stabilization. In this paper, we provide a rigorous justification. More specifically, we prove by construction that if a switched linear system admits a stabilizing full-information controller, with access to the entire history of states and switching signals, then a memoryless and homogeneous of degree one stabilizing controller also exists. Specifically, in the modeindependent setting the controller can be chosen to depend only on the current state, and in the mode-dependent setting only on the current state and active mode. Our results thus show that dynamic controllers offer no additional stabilizing capability for switched linear systems, formally validating this folklore claim.
tldr: This paper proves that memoryless feedback controllers are sufficient for stabilizing switched linear systems, contradicting the need for dynamic controllers.
motivation: To resolve a long-standing assumption in switched linear systems theory about whether dynamic controllers offer additional stabilizing capability over static ones.
method: The authors constructively prove that if a stabilizing full-information controller exists, then a memoryless, homogeneous of degree one controller also exists, using rigorous mathematical analysis.
result: Memoryless controllers (depending only on current state or current state and mode) are as powerful as dynamic controllers for stabilization of switched linear systems.
conclusion: The results formally validate the folklore claim that dynamic controllers are unnecessary for stabilization, simplifying controller design for switched systems.

title: Graph Neural Networks For Community Detection In Graph Signal Analysis
authors: Roberto Cavoretto, Alessandra de Rossi, Enrico Montini
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Community detection is a central problem in graph analysis, with applications ranging from network science to graph signal processing. In recent years, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as effective tools for learning low-dimensional representations of graph-structured data and have shown strong performance in clustering tasks, particularly on large and high-dimensional graphs. This paper investigates the use of GNN-based community detection within a graph signal interpolation framework. After reviewing the main classes of GNN architectures for community detection according to a standard taxonomy, we integrate the resulting graph communities into a Partition of Unity Method (PUM) for interpolation with Graph Basis Functions (GBFs). In this approach, GNN-derived communities are used to construct local subdomains on which GBF interpolants are computed and subsequently combined into a global approximation. Numerical experiments on benchmark %graph datasets, including geometric and urban network examples demonstrate that the proposed combination of GNN-based clustering and GBF-PUM interpolation yields accurate signal reconstructions. The results indicate that deep learning-based community detection can provide effective graph partitions for localized interpolation schemes, supporting its use in scalable graph signal analysis.
tldr: This paper uses Graph Neural Networks for community detection to improve graph signal interpolation via a Partition of Unity Method with Graph Basis Functions.
motivation: To enhance graph signal interpolation by leveraging GNN-based community detection to create effective local subdomains.
method: GNNs are used for community detection, then communities are integrated into a Partition of Unity Method with Graph Basis Functions for interpolation.
result: Numerical experiments on benchmark datasets show that GNN-based clustering combined with GBF-PUM yields accurate signal reconstructions.
conclusion: Deep learning-based community detection can provide effective graph partitions for localized interpolation, supporting scalable graph signal analysis.

title: Fast Spawn\&Prune (fs\&p): Global Convergence Of Stochastic Conic Particle Gradient Descent Via Birth/death Process
authors: Yohann de Castro (ICJ, ECL, IUF, PSPM), S\'ebastien Gadat (tse-R, IUF), Cl\'ement Marteau
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the global optimization of the objective function arising in continuous sparse regression, specifically the Beurling LASSO (BLASSO), over the space of measures. While Conic Particle Gradient Descent (CPGD) methods are computationally efficient, they may become trapped in local minima due to the non-convexity of the parameterization. To overcome this limitation, we introduce Fast Spawn\&Prune (FS\&P), a stochastic algorithm that extends FastPart introduced in De Castro et al. (2025) and combines CPGD with a birth-death process. The birth mechanism ensures asymptotic global exploration by introducing particles in regions where first-order optimality conditions are violated, while the death process preserves computational efficiency by pruning non-informative particles. We provide the first theoretical guarantee of global convergence for this class of discrete-time stochastic algorithms, without requiring exponentially large initializations. Furthermore, we derive explicit convergence rates for the excess risk, which scale as [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the number of iterations and d the dimension of the domain, thereby quantifying the trade-off between global exploration and local refinement. Moreover, the sample complexity is [MATH] (up to logarithmic factors). We also propose a horizon-free variant that does not require prior knowledge of the iteration budget.
tldr: This paper introduces a stochastic algorithm for global optimization of the Beurling LASSO objective, combining conic particle gradient descent with a birth-death process to avoid local minima.
motivation: Conic Particle Gradient Descent methods are efficient but can get trapped in local minima due to non-convex parameterization; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The Fast Spawn&Prune (FS&P) algorithm extends FastPart by adding a birth-death process: birth introduces particles where optimality conditions are violated, death removes non-informative particles.
result: First theoretical guarantee of global convergence for this class of discrete-time stochastic algorithms without exponentially large initializations, with explicit convergence rates scaling as O(1/√k + √(d/k)) and sample complexity O(d log k).
conclusion: The algorithm provides a principled way to balance global exploration and local refinement, with a horizon-free variant that does not require prior knowledge of iteration budget.

title: Spa-mae: A Physics-Guided Csi Foundation Model For Wireless Physical Layer
authors: Chen Chen, Weijie Jin, Hengtao He, Xiaoheng Sun, Shi Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning (DL) has been widely used in future 6G physical layer communications, but task-specific DL models are difficult to generalize across different physical layer tasks. Recently emerging wireless foundation models demonstrate strong generalization capability. However, existing methods mainly adapt pretrained language/vision models or rely on CSI reconstruction objectives for pretraining, with limited use of channel knowledge, and thus have limited performance. To address this limitation, we propose SPA-MAE, a physics-guided wireless foundation model by exploiting the adapted MAE backbone and channel knowledge. A physical prior module is developed to provide two complementary guidance signals in the pretraining stage. Specifically, the parameter-aware guidance branch extracts features from explicit multipath parameters and encourages the encoder output to align them, while the structure-aware guidance branch encourages the encoder to capture the sparse transformed-domain CSI structure obtained after a 2D FFT. After end-to-end learning, the MAE encoder will be retained for downstream tasks. Experiments on four wireless tasks show that SPA-MAE outperforms state-of-the-art CSI foundation models with smaller number of parameters, especially under low-SNR and limited-data conditions.
tldr: A physics-guided foundation model for wireless channel state information (CSI) processing is proposed, leveraging MAE and channel knowledge to improve generalization across physical layer tasks.
motivation: Existing wireless foundation models adapt pretrained language/vision models or rely on CSI reconstruction, with limited use of channel knowledge, leading to suboptimal performance.
method: The authors develop SPA-MAE, which incorporates a physical prior module with two guidance branches: parameter-aware (aligning encoder output with explicit multipath parameters) and structure-aware (encouraging capture of sparse transformed-domain CSI structure after 2D FFT).
result: SPA-MAE outperforms state-of-the-art CSI foundation models on four wireless tasks with fewer parameters, especially under low-SNR and limited-data conditions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the benefit of integrating domain-specific physical knowledge into foundation models for wireless communications, suggesting a promising direction for future 6G systems.

title: When Can A Neural Operator Replace A Coarse Solve? Architectural Principles For Two-level Preconditioning
authors: Hugo Melchers, Michael Abdelmalik, Victorita Dolean
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural operators are increasingly used as drop-in accelerators inside classical numerical methods, but it is rarely clear which architectural ingredients matter for which role. We answer this question for one important role: the coarse-space correction inside a two-level preconditioner for discretised linear partial differential equations. By systematically varying four DeepONet-like architectures along two design axes - input discretisation (sampling versus integration against a basis) and source-term linearity - we show that the favourable corner of this 2[MATH]2 design is occupied by a single architecture, the Neural Green's Operator (NGO), and that moving away from it produces predictable failure modes: structurally non-symmetric preconditioned spectra, breakdown of preconditioned conjugate gradients on self-adjoint problems, and stagnation on non-self-adjoint ones. Used as a coarse-space correction, the NGO matches the iteration count of an exact coarse solve on diffusion and advection-diffusion problems. We also characterise the failure of fixed-size learned coarse spaces at high Helmholtz wave numbers, isolating it as a property of the basis rather than of the architecture. The principle generalises: integrating inputs against the basis used for the output is what allows a neural operator to serve as a Galerkin-type coarse-space correction.
tldr: This paper studies neural operator architectures for coarse-space correction in two-level preconditioners for PDEs, finding that the Neural Green's Operator (NGO) is optimal due to its input discretization and linearity properties.
motivation: To determine which architectural ingredients of neural operators are crucial when used as drop-in accelerators for coarse-space correction in numerical PDE solvers.
method: Systematically varied four DeepONet-like architectures along two design axes (input discretization and source-term linearity) and tested them as coarse-space corrections in two-level preconditioners for diffusion, advection-diffusion, and Helmholtz problems.
result: The Neural Green's Operator (NGO) uniquely achieves symmetric preconditioned spectra and matches exact coarse solve iteration counts; other architectures cause breakdown of conjugate gradients or stagnation.
conclusion: Integrating inputs against the basis used for output is essential for a neural operator to serve as a Galerkin-type coarse-space correction; fixed-size learned coarse spaces fail at high Helmholtz wave numbers due to basis limitations.

title: Constraint-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Networks For Seir Reaction-Diffusion Epidemic Models With Vital Dynamics
authors: Matthias Ehrhardt Achraf Zinihi
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reaction-diffusion epidemic models with vital dynamics are an important framework for describing the spatial and temporal spread of infectious diseases. In this work, we present a constraint-aware, physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach to an SEIR reaction-diffusion system with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Due to the scarcity of spatial epidemiological datasets, we generate synthetic benchmark data using structure-preserving implicit-explicit nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) schemes that ensure positivity, boundedness, and numerical stability. The PINN framework integrates PDE residuals, observational data, boundary conditions, and epidemiological constraints within a unified optimization procedure. Specifically, the loss function incorporates the non-negativity of compartment populations and the admissibility of epidemiological parameters. We apply the method to forward simulation and inverse parameter estimation in one- and two-dimensional settings. Numerical experiments demonstrate the framework's ability to accurately reconstruct spatiotemporal epidemic dynamics and reliably identify parameters, even when data is sparse or noisy. These results underscore the potential of constraint-aware PINNs as a robust, data-driven methodology for spatial epidemic modeling.
tldr: This paper applies physics-informed neural networks to SEIR reaction-diffusion epidemic models, focusing on constraint-aware training for forward simulation and inverse parameter estimation.
motivation: To address the scarcity of spatial epidemiological data and the need for robust, data-driven methods that respect physical and epidemiological constraints.
method: A constraint-aware PINN framework that integrates PDE residuals, observational data, boundary conditions, and epidemiological constraints (non-negativity, parameter admissibility) into a unified loss function; synthetic data generated by structure-preserving NSFD schemes.
result: The method accurately reconstructs spatiotemporal epidemic dynamics and reliably identifies parameters even with sparse or noisy data in 1D and 2D settings.
conclusion: Constraint-aware PINNs are a promising methodology for spatial epidemic modeling, with potential for extension to more complex models and real-world data.

title: Adaptive Reduced-Basis Trust-Region Methods For Defect Identification In Elastic Materials
authors: Benedikt Klein, Mario Ohlberger, Thomas Schuster
abstract: ArXiv:2605.19896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monitoring the integrity of elastic structures using ultrasonic waves requires the efficient identification of material parameters from measured surface displacements. The displacement field is governed by Cauchy's equation of motion, i.e., an elastic wave equation. Consequently, defect localization leads to a high-dimensional spatial parameter identification problem for a hyperbolic system with given initial and boundary conditions. Stable parameter reconstructions typically rely on regularization techniques such as the iteratively regularized Gauss--Newton method (IRGNM). However, its practical application is computationally demanding due to the high-dimensional nature of the problem. To address this bottleneck, we propose a reduced-order modeling approach that simultaneously reduces the state and parameter spaces using adaptively constructed reduced-basis spaces. This yields online-efficient surrogate models for both the forward and adjoint evaluations required in derivative-based optimization. To ensure reliability, the IRGNM iteration is embedded into an adaptive, trust-region framework that provides accuracy of the reduced-order approximations. The approach extends our recent contributions, which focus on elliptic and parabolic problems, to the hyperbolic setting. We demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the method for defect detection through numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper presents a reduced-order modeling approach for defect identification in elastic materials using ultrasonic waves, focusing on computational efficiency for hyperbolic PDE-constrained optimization.
motivation: Defect localization in elastic structures via ultrasonic waves leads to high-dimensional parameter identification problems that are computationally demanding with standard regularization techniques.
method: The authors propose an adaptive reduced-basis trust-region method that simultaneously reduces state and parameter spaces, embedding the iteratively regularized Gauss-Newton method into a trust-region framework to ensure accuracy.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the method for defect detection in elastic materials, extending previous work from elliptic/parabolic to hyperbolic settings.
conclusion: The approach provides online-efficient surrogate models for forward and adjoint evaluations, enabling practical defect identification, with potential extensions to other hyperbolic inverse problems.
